2609.23877.title: Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery
2609.23877.paper_summary: Modern music streaming platforms face a persistent tradeoff: exploiting familiar content versus driving the exploration of novel items. While users frequently desire discovery, they hesitate to select unknown artists over proven favorites. Providing transparent, natural language rationales that explain why an unexplored item is recommended lowers this barrier. However, while Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at this nuanced explainability, their real-time deployment is severely bottlenecked by prohibitive inference costs and computational overhead. In this paper, we present an industry case study of a decoupled recommendation architecture that successfully scales exploration without compromising latency. Our system isolates LLM inference asynchronously offline, pre-computing personalized candidate pools of undiscovered artists alongside tailored rationales. Large-scale online A/B experiments validate our design. We demonstrate that combining LLM-backed recommendations with these explanatory rationales significantly reduces the trust barrier for new content, yielding statistically significant improvements in both user exploration and overall engagement on the discovery surfaces.
2609.23877.paper_summary_zh: 現代音樂串流平台面臨著一個持續的權衡：利用熟悉的內容與推動探索新項目之間的平衡。雖然用戶經常渴望發現新事物，但他們卻猶豫不決，選擇未知的藝術家而非已知的喜愛者。提供透明的自然語言理由，解釋為何推薦未探索的項目，可以降低這一障礙。然而，儘管大型語言模型（LLMs）在這種細緻的可解釋性方面表現出色，但其實時部署卻受到高昂推理成本和計算開銷的嚴重瓶頸。在本文中，我們呈現了一個行業案例研究，展示了一種解耦的推薦架構，成功地在不妥協延遲的情況下擴展探索。我們的系統異步離線隔離LLM推理，預先計算個性化的未發現藝術家候選池及其量身定制的理由。大規模的在線A/B實驗驗證了我們的設計。我們展示了結合LLM支持的推薦與這些解釋性理由顯著降低了對新內容的信任障礙，並在用戶探索和整體參與度方面在發現界面上取得了統計上顯著的改善。
